newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn ends up on export data, acreage talk.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn ends up on export data, acreage talk.

text.p: CBOT corn futures closed higher on bullish export data plus talk about potential reductions in U.S. corn acreage this year, traders said.

"It's not acting badly at all. It was just a technical correction (Wednesday's break). It acts super I think," said Vic Lespinasse of Dean Witter. "It was a technical correction and now it's coming back and the export sales were good."
USDA Thursday said U.S. net export sales of corn during the week ended March 6 totaled 1.009 million tonnes, above expectations for 700,000 to 800,000 tonnes.
There were rumblings corn acreage may be reduced.

USDA estimated at its recently completed Agriculture Outlook Conference that U.S. corn acreage this year would total roughly 81 million acres. Fertilizer producer IMC Global Inc earlier Thursday said its survey indicated corn acreage at 81 million acres. But there was floor talk that Memphis-based analytical firm Sparks Companies on Friday would peg the acreage tally below the 81-million mark.
Concerns about wet weather and flooding in the U.S. eastern Midwest also boosted the market, traders said.
Corn closed 1-1/2 to 6-3/4 cents per bushel higher, with March up three at $3.00-3/4 and December up 6-1/4 at $2.87.
Corn rallied in late trading on agressive buying in the December contract led by FIMAT Futures purchase of ten million bushels of that contract, traders said.
Gains in corn were curbed by indications China is increasing its corn sales on the world market and on signals the market remained technically overbought for the short term.

Technicians early Thursday said first resistance in the March contract was at $3.05 and second resistance was at $3.16. The session high was $3.01-1/2. First support was at $2.94 and second support was at $2.83. The session low for the March was $2.95-1/4.
Chartists said the four- and 20-day moving averages for the March were giving off bullish signals.
The short term nine-day relative strength index (RSI) for the March closed at 55 percent. The market considers an RSI of 70 or more as overbought and 30 or less as oversold.
Corn futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 85,000 contracts, below the 101,443 traded Wednesday.
In corn options, E.D. and F. Man International bought 1,600 May $2.70 puts at 1-3/4 to 1-7/8 cents, traders said.
Corn options volume was estimated at 17,000 contracts, below the 18,806 traded Wednesday.
